title: Constant geometric stalks and point-transport Frobenius are the coefficient unit
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_m=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Equip the constant finite coefficient sheaves $(A_m)_Y$, their completed integral unit $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, and its rationalization $E_Y$ with the canonical geometric Weil comparisons of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]: at the integral and rational levels $\theta_{\mathcal O_E}$ and $\theta_E$, and at the finite level $\theta_m=c_m\circ\lambda_m:Lg_Y^*(A_m)_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}(A_m)_Y$, where $c_m$ is the finite-level structure isomorphism of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure] and $\lambda_m$ the identification of the derived pullback along the isomorphism $g_Y$ with the inverse image [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Write $g_Y,g_s$ for geometric Galois Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed].

For every $n\ge1$, every $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and every geometric point $\bar x:s\to Y$ obtained from an embedding $\mathbf F_{q^n}\hookrightarrow k$, the return is $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$. Use the actual point transports $\iota$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], their iterates $I^{[n]}$, the specified pullback-composition comparisons, and the iterated canonical Weil maps to form the local operators of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] at finite, integral and rational levels. There are canonical coefficient-unit identifications
$$\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*(A_m)_Y)\simeq A_m[0],\qquad
\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})\simeq\mathcal O_E[0],\qquad
\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*E_Y)\simeq E[0].$$
Under these identifications the composite local operators are respectively $1_{A_m[0]}$, $1_{\mathcal O_E[0]}$ and $1_{E[0]}$. The identifications and operator equalities commute with every reduction $A_{m+1}\to A_m$, the projections of the completed integral unit to the finite levels, and rationalization $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $B_{T,m}=(A_m)_T$ and $B_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$. The image of any embedding $\mathbf F_{q^n}\hookrightarrow k$ is the unique subfield with $q^n$ elements, so $\gamma^n$ fixes this image pointwise: it is the inverse of the $q^n$-power automorphism. Writing the point as $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n}\to Y_0$ together with its $k$-coordinate, applying $g_Y^n$ changes only the latter coordinate by $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^n)$. Applying $g_s^n$ changes both coordinates, but leaves the $\mathbf F_{q^n}$-coordinate unchanged. The two composites therefore agree by the universal property of $Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. This proves $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$, without asserting that either composite equals $\bar x$.

source.place: Constant-sheaf clause; agent expansion of reviewed step 5

proof.text:
For any scheme map $f:T\to V$, the finite-level coefficient comparison is the canonical multiplication map
$$d_{f,m}:Lf_m^*B_{V,m}=f^{-1}B_{V,m}\otimes_{f^{-1}B_{V,m}}B_{T,m}\longrightarrow B_{T,m},\qquad z\otimes b\longmapsto c^{f}_{A_m}(z)b.$$
Its inverse sends $b$ to $1\otimes b$. These formulas respect the balancing relation and are inverse, since $z\otimes b=1\otimes c^{f}_{A_m}(z)b$. The coefficient ring map is an isomorphism by prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map; the finite derived pullback is the exact module inverse image specified in def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, so these are computations of the actual derived maps on coefficient objects in degree zero. At $f=\bar x$ this identifies $L\bar x^*B_{Y,m}$ with $B_{s,m}[0]$. The finite-constant sections formula gives $\Gamma(s,B_{s,m})=C(|s|,A_m)=A_m$, by evaluation at the unique point of $s$. Thus the finite coefficient-unit identification sends $a\in A_m$ to the constant-section class $a$ in degree zero. The point fibre is precisely this sections functor.

source.place: Constant-sheaf clause; agent expansion of reviewed step 5

proof.text: The canonical unit maps respect the specified finite pullback compositors. Indeed, lem-pur-proetale-constant-ring-composition gives the equality of the coefficient maps for two successive inverse images. On the corresponding tensor representatives the compositor then sends $(z\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $z\otimes c^h_{A_m}(b)c$; applying the two multiplication maps of step 2 gives $c^{kh}_{A_m}(z)c^h_{A_m}(b)c$ on both sides. These formulas apply sheafwise, since tensors are locally generated by pure tensors. The specified derived compositor is this termwise map on a K-flat flat-term model; the rank-one coefficient object is such a model. For an isomorphism $f$, its finite $\lambda_m$ is $z\otimes b\mapsto(c^f_{A_m})^{-1}(b)z$, so $c^f_{A_m}\lambda_m=d_{f,m}$. In particular the canonical finite Weil map is $d_{g_Y,m}$. Induction on $r$ now identifies $\theta_m^{[r]}$ with $d_{g_Y^r,m}$: the base $r=1$ is the preceding formula; the step substitutes the induction hypothesis in $\theta_m^{[r+1]}=\theta_m^{[r]}L(g_Y^r)^*\theta_m$ and applies the just-verified composition identity.

source.place: Constant-sheaf clause; agent expansion of reviewed step 5

proof.text: Compute the point transport on $B_{s,m}[0]$ using its actual recipe. Restriction along $g_s$ sends a constant section $a$ to the same constant section $a$ on $(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)$. Insertion into the inverse-image colimit and sheafification sends it to the inverse-image constant class; the adjoint structure map $c^{g_s}_{A_m}$ sends that class to $a$, by its defining constant-section formula. The map $\kappa$ sends the class to its tensor with $1$, and $d_{g_s,m}$ sends that tensor back to $a$. Hence $\Gamma(s,d_{g_s,m})\iota_{B_{s,m}}$ is the identity on every $a\in A_m$. Naturality of $\iota$ lets us make the same computation after each unit identification from step 2. Induction, using the compositor calculation of step 3, proves that $I^{[r]}$ followed by $d_{g_s^r,m}$ is the identity in unit coordinates for every $r\ge1$. The middle comparison in the local operator uses the equality from step 1; both paths through this square have the unit identifications of step 3 and therefore act as $a\mapsto a$. Finally $L\bar x^*\theta_m^{[n]}$ acts as the unit multiplication by step 3. Every arrow of the local composite thus preserves the coefficient coordinate, proving that the finite local operator is $1_{A_m[0]}$.

source.place: Constant-sheaf clause; agent expansion of reviewed step 5

proof.text: These calculations commute with the coefficient reductions as actual maps of finite systems. A reduction sends $z\otimes b$ to $\bar z\otimes\bar b$ and $a$ to $\bar a$. The equality $r_m c^{f}_{A_{m+1}}=c^{f}_{A_m}f^{-1}(r_m)$ for isomorphisms, and the defining constant-section formula for arbitrary $f$, show that the multiplication maps and their inverses commute with reduction. Restriction and the inverse-image colimit coprojections commute with the sheaf maps induced by $r_m$; $\kappa$ commutes because $\overline{z\otimes1}=\bar z\otimes1$. The tensor-compositor formula of step 3 commutes because reduction is a ring homomorphism. Thus the finite local identities of step 4 are the identity of the whole strict coefficient system, not a choice of unrelated equalities at its individual levels.

source.place: Constant-sheaf clause; agent expansion of reviewed step 5

proof.text:
Use $B_Y[0]$ itself as a flat-term K-flat model for the integral unit: tensoring with the free rank-one module is the identity. Its canonical derived reductions are $B_{Y,m}[0]$, by lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible. The integral pullback formula in def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom and the compatible multiplication maps of steps 2 and 5 therefore identify $L\bar x^*B_Y$ with the strict quotient cone $H(B_{s,\bullet})=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$. The identity-extension comparison of lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison, applied to the derived-complete coefficient unit $B_s$, is the isomorphism $\chi_s:B_s[0]\to H(B_{s,\bullet})$, $b\mapsto(0,(\pi_m b)_m)$. Define the integral unit identification by its inverse after the preceding strict-cone identification. This specifies the entire derived map, and identifies every projection with the quotient map. These objects lie in the required bounded constructible categories by lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible. Limits of sheaves are sectionwise, so the finite sections formula of step 2 gives
$$\Gamma(s,B_s)=\varprojlim_m\Gamma(s,B_{s,m})=\varprojlim_m A_m=R.$$
For the last equality use completeness of $E$: representatives $a_m\in R$ of a compatible residue sequence satisfy $a_{m+1}-a_m\in\varpi_E^mR$ and hence form a Cauchy sequence. Its limit $a$ lies in the closed unit ball $R$, and $a-a_m\in\varpi_E^mR$; uniqueness follows from $\bigcap_m\varpi_E^mR=0$, since $|\varpi_E|_E<1$. Conversely $a$ gives its residue sequence. These inverse maps are the canonical constant-value map and the limit map, so their $m$-th projections are precisely $a\mapsto a\bmod\varpi_E^m$. Since $\operatorname{Fib}_s=\Gamma(s,-)$ integrally, this proves the integral coefficient-unit identification with $R[0]$ and its projection compatibility.

source.place: Constant-sheaf clause; agent expansion of reviewed step 5

proof.text: Use the specified whole-tower realization, rather than detecting arbitrary derived morphisms by their finite reductions. For $g=g_Y$ and $g=g_s$, lem-pod-canonical-coefficient-pullback-reduction identifies the canonical $\lambda_R$ with $\kappa_{B}^{-1}$ and gives $\pi_m(c_R\lambda_R)=(c_m\lambda_m)\rho_m$. Thus the integral canonical Weil map is the realized finite multiplication map, with the actual quotient-cone normalization. Lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization specifies the integral compositors as realizations of the finite tensor compositors, including the comparisons for successive pullbacks; its construction is natural, unital, associative, and respects equality of scheme morphisms. Consequently steps 2--3, for the unit models of step 6, identify the iterated integral Weil map and the middle return comparison with the realizations of their finite system maps. For the point transport apply lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-powers to the coefficient system $C_m=B_{s,m}[0]$, whose derived limit is the constructible coefficient unit by lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible and the identity-extension completeness comparison of lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison. That lemma identifies $I^{[n]}$ with the realization of the specified finite transports, including the same compositors. Its naturality allows the unit replacement $L\bar x^*B_Y\simeq B_s$ from step 6. The entire integral local composite is therefore the realization of the identity system map established in steps 4--5. Functoriality sends that identity to the identity. In the coordinates of step 6 this is $1_{R[0]}$, and its projections to $A_m[0]$ are the finite identities because all unit and realization maps just used have the specified quotient projections.

source.place: Constant-sheaf clause; agent expansion of reviewed step 5

proof.text: Finally rationalize the integral calculation. By def-weil-rationalization-karoubi and def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, the rational coefficient object, Weil map and pullback comparisons are the images of their integral versions; by def-weil-frobenius-point-transport its rational point transport is $\iota^R\otimes_RE$. The point fibre is $\Gamma(s,-)\otimes_RE$, so the integral unit identification becomes $R[0]\otimes_RE\simeq E[0]$, by $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. The local composite becomes $1_{R[0]}\otimes1=1_{E[0]}$, since scalar extension preserves identities and composition. The map to rational coefficients is $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, which under multiplication is the inclusion $R\hookrightarrow E$. Together with the explicit projections $a\mapsto a\bmod\varpi_E^m$ of step 6 and the strict reduction squares of step 5, this is exactly the claimed compatibility with reductions, completed-unit projections and rationalization. No torsion module $A_m$ is tensor-rationalized to obtain the rational unit.

The closure of neither reaches a trace-formula or Poincaré theorem or an assumption leaf, so both are accepted, as lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization was in the Q60 ruling. Steps: step 1, the return g_Y^n x̄ = x̄ g_s^n, follows from the unique-subfield lemma. Step 2 gives the finite unit d_{f,m} through prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map and the constant-sections formula (Γ = A_m). Step 3 checks the tensor compositor, shows c_mλ_m = d by the pod lemma's finite λ_n formula, and identifies θ^{[r]} by an induction with base and step written out. Step 4 computes the transport res, ins, c, κ, d as a ↦ a, with naturality for the iterates. Step 5 checks strict compatibility with reductions. Step 6: R_s is derived complete, χ for L=E is the strict-cone unit, and lim A_m = O_E by completeness. Step 7: the pod normalization, the trf compositor realization and the trf power transport with N=B_s ∈ D^b_c match the ν/κ^{-1} normalization. Step 8: rationalization is ⊗E with no torsion ⊗E. I tested the empty scheme, Spec F_q, degree d | n, m=1, ramified E and nonseparated or nonreduced Y_0. No duplicates: I checked pod-frobenius-fixes-unit-section, pur-twist-frobenius-scalar, zl-normalized-coefficient-unit-realization and the stalk lemma. All 13 off-unit tool uses are declared, and the unit cites sk-thm-trace-transport.
